title: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It
body: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It An AI-defined fab uses accelerated simulation, learned physics models and AI agents to give engineers faster answers across design, testing and manufacturing. November 3, 2026 by Timothy Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking. For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days. Physical experiments on a fab line are slow and expensive. A wrong call on yield or process quality has real consequences. AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast. Accelerated computing shortens simulation time, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before committing to physical trials. Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time. AI agents handle sequences of engineering tasks that once consumed hours. And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle. Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers. Shorter Simulation Cycles Change What Engineers Can Explore Accelerated computing doesn’t just speed up individual calculations — it changes how many alternatives engineers can test before committing. Multiphysics simulations model interactions among physical effects, such as heat transfer, electrical behavior and mechanical stress. Using the NVIDIA cuDSS library, multiphysics software provider COMSOL is accelerating such simulations for semiconductor manufacturing by up to 10x. This helps engineers optimize equipment and processes, compare alternatives and decide which changes to test physically. Applied Materials and NVIDIA are collaborating to accelerate atomic-scale materials discovery and process development. By integrating NVIDIA cuDSS, Applied’s Ginestra simulation platform runs up to 10x faster than CPU-only approaches. And with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo, Applied’s ACE+ multiphysics platform delivers topography simulations up to 35x faster. In some cases, acceleration doesn’t just shorten the calculation — it enables it altogether. Computational lithography — which defines how circuit patterns are printed onto silicon — involves calculations too intensive to complete on CPU at production scale. Siemens is integrating NVIDIA cuLitho into its Calibre lithography software, delivering up to 17x acceleration on key simulation workloads. That expands what engineers can verify before a wafer goes to print. As such, faster calculations can help researchers explore material behavior and reaction pathways that influence next-generation semiconductor processes. Predicting Process Behavior Without Running Every Simulation In addition to accelerating simulations, AI trained on physics can predict how materials and processes will behave — without running a full simulation each time. The payoff is most visible in complex calculations that are expensive even on accelerated hardware. Plasma — the electrically charged gas used in semiconductor etch processes — is one example. Modeling plasma behavior requires solving equations that capture how electrical, chemical and thermal processes interact, making repeated simulation costly. Lam Research demonstrated that the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework can predict plasma behavior in milliseconds, compared with days for a full simulation — giving engineers a faster way to explore process conditions without rerunning the full model each time. Applied Materials uses digital twins built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to simulate fab-level optimizations in layout, throughput, cost and process control. Agents Handle the Steps Between Decisions Engineers turn analyses into decisions — revising a design, investigating a test failure, adjusting a production process and more. AI agents can help carry out the steps between those decisions. Evaluating which AI model to apply to a given task is one example: a sequential, manual process that can consume hours on the test floor. Advantest is using NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard AI agents to automate that selection, reducing response times from hours to minutes. Testing Factory Changes Before They Reach the Line Digital twins let teams simulate equipment configurations, layouts and process changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. This reduces experimentation costs, especially as fabs become more complex and the stakes of a wrong change get higher. A photorealistic fab digital twin built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, used to simulate material flow, spot bottlenecks and validate operational strategies before deployment. Image courtesy of Applied Materials. Applied Materials uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build physically accurate digital twins of entire fabs. Teams can simulate material movement, identify bottlenecks and evaluate layouts and operating strategies — extending virtual experimentation beyond individual processes to how the factory works as a whole. The Connected Loop The future of semiconductor manufacturing lies in connecting these capabilities: using production data to inform models and models to evaluate changes, then bringing those findings back to the engineers making production decisions. That’s the promise of the AI-defined fab: where AI helps people learn from each production cycle and act on that knowledge sooner. Explore how NVIDIA is working with semiconductor leaders across the chip lifecycle. title: Former U.S. Government Contractor Pleads Guilty to Spying for Ethiopia
body: Press Release Former U.S. Government Contractor Pleads Guilty to Spying for Ethiopia Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON – Abraham Teklu Lemma, 54, a former information technology contractor at the U.S. Department of State, the U.S. Department of Justice, and the National Reconnaissance Office, pleaded guilty today to conspiring to commit espionage on behalf of the government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “For more than two years, Lemma exploited a position of trust to provide highly classified U.S. government information to a foreign government,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “In doing so, he betrayed his oath, his colleagues, and his country, while jeopardizing our national security. His guilty plea sends a clear message: those who compromise America’s most sensitive secrets will be investigated, prosecuted, and held accountable.” Senior Judge John D. Bates scheduled sentencing for April 14, 2027. “Lemma betrayed the United States to an extraordinary degree,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “He exploited his IT administrator access to remove classified national defense information, including Top Secret information, from a secure facility and transmitted it to Ethiopian government officials hoping they would use it to target and kill paramilitary fighters in a regional conflict. Clearance holders pledge undivided loyalty to the United States and bear a legal and moral responsibility to protect classified information. Those who betray this trust will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.” “Today’s guilty plea makes clear that any attempt to betray the United States, violate the trust of the American people, and compromise our national security will not be tolerated,” said Assistant Director in Charge Darren B. Cox of the FBI Washington Field Office. “Lemma abused his position of trust and access to some of our nation’s most highly classified information, conspiring with foreign government officials to unlawfully disclose materials protected to the highest level. In doing so, he not only endangered our national security but also betrayed the trust placed in him by the American people.” According to court papers, Lemma, of Silver Spring, Maryland, held a Top Secret U.S. security clearance who, from 2021 until his arrest in August 2023, conspired with senior Ethiopian government officials to collect and transmit dozens of highly classified documents, notes, materials, and photographs, classified up to the Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) level, to Ethiopian government officials. Material identified as “Top Secret” means that unauthorized disclosure of the material is reasonably to cause “exceptionally grave damage to the national security” of the United States. Much of the highly classified information Lemma shared with the Ethiopian government concerned an armed conflict in Ethiopia. Lemma’s conspirators included senior officials within political, military, and intelligence branches of the Ethiopian government. During his espionage activities, Lemma took numerous steps to conceal his conduct. and surreptitiously removed classified documents and information from U.S. government holdings. Specifically, Lemma wrote notes by hand with classified information and then hand-carried those notes out of secure U.S. government facilities.  Additionally, as an IT administrator, Lemma removed electronic versions of classified information from classified U.S. government repositories and then removed the same classified information from secure U.S. government facilities where he worked. On some occasions, Lemma encouraged his Ethiopian government conspirators to take direct action against paramilitary groups who were fighting the government of Ethiopia. For example, on Dec. 18, 2021, Lemma told one conspirator, “We have to finish these people once and for all, otherwise there will never be peace in Ethiopia.” Later that day, Lemma shared additional information with his conspirator and wrote, “Please send Dro[nes].” According to the plea agreement, Lemma agreed to plead guilty to conspiracy to transmit national defense information to a foreign government, in violation of 18 U.S.C. §794.  If accepted by the Court, Lemma has agreed to be incarcerated for a period of between 120 and 262 months. The investigation was conducted by the FBI Washington Field Office. The matter is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Tejpal Chawla and Adam P. Barry for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia, and Trial Attorney Kathryn DeMarco of the Department of Justice’s National Security Division. 24cr573 Follow us on X , Instagram , and YouTube Or at https://www.justice.gov/usao-dc Updated November 3, 2026 Topic National Security Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - District of Columbia

title: Strand Book Store, Inc. to Pay Nearly $1.5 Million for Improper Receipt of Paycheck Protection Program Loan
body: Press Release Strand Book Store, Inc. to Pay Nearly $1.5 Million for Improper Receipt of Paycheck Protection Program Loan Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON – The United States Attorney for the District of Columbia announced today that Strand Book Store, Inc. has agreed to pay $1,482,560 because the New York City bookstore violated the False Claims Act by improperly applying for and receiving a second draw loan under the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) for which it was not eligible. Strand was ineligible because Senator Ron Wyden’s wife was the owner. “The Paycheck Protection Program was created to save American jobs, not to enrich those who aren’t eligible for taxpayer-funded relief, especially the wife of a U.S. Senator,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Strand Book Store, owned by Nancy Bass Wyden, wife of U.S. Senator Ron Wyden, received $932,350 in second draw PPP funds despite a federal law barring businesses controlled by a member of Congress or their spouse from receiving those loans. Our Fraud and Asset Recovery Division will expose this abuse, pursue those who exploit taxpayer dollars, and hold them accountable. No one gets a pass when it comes to defrauding the American taxpayer.” When Congress enacted the Coronavirus, Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act in March 2020, it authorized forgivable PPP loans to eligible small businesses and nonprofit organizations for job retention and certain other expenses. The PPP loan program was administered by the Small Business Administration. In the Economic Aid to Hard-Hit Small Businesses, Nonprofits, and Venues Act enacted in December 2020, Congress provided additional funding for PPP loans and allowed eligible entities to apply for a “second draw” of PPP funding. The Economic Aid Act included a prohibition against businesses obtaining second draw PPP funds if a member of Congress or their spouse directly or indirectly held a controlling interest in the PPP loan applicant. In February 2021, Strand applied for a second draw PPP loan in the amount of $932,350. At the time, the controlling owner of Strand was Nancy Bass Wyden, the wife of U.S. Senator Ron Wyden. On behalf of Strand, Ms. Wyden made a number of certifications as part of the loan application, including that the spouse of a Member of Congress does not directly or indirectly hold a controlling interest in the applicant. Ms. Wyden’s certification was knowingly and materially false and Strand was not eligible for the second draw loan it received. The settlement resolves claims brought under the qui tam or whistleblower provisions of the False Claims Act. Under these provisions, a private party can file an action on behalf of the United States and receive a portion of the recovery. The qui tam complaint was filed by a corporate Relator Blockquote Inc. and is captioned U.S. ex rel. Blockquote Inc. v. Strand Book Store, Inc., Civ. No. 25-3609 (D.D.C.) . Blockquote Inc. will receive a total share of approximately $148,256 in connection with the settlement. The civil settlement resulted from an investigation by Assistant United States Attorney Sean M. Tepe with the support of attorney Christopher J. McClintock of SBA’s Office of the General Counsel. This is the second recovery on behalf of the United States since U.S. Attorney Pirro announced the creation of the Fraud and Asset Recovery Division, headed by Assistant U.S. Attorney Dan Schiffer. Tips and complaint regarding potential fraud affecting COVID-19 government relief programs can be reported by calling the Department of Justice’s National Center for Disaster Fraud (NCDF) Hotline at (866) 720-5721 or by submitting a NCDF Web Complaint form at https://www.justice.gov/disaster-fraud/ncdf-disaster-complaint-form . On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The claims resolved by the civil settlement are allegations only, and there has been no determination of liability. ## 25cv3609 Follow us on X , Instagram , and YouTube or at https://www.justice.gov/usao-dc Updated November 3, 2026 Topics Benefit Fraud COVID-Related Fraud Component USAO - District of Columbia

Strand was ineligible because Senator Ron Wyden’s wife was the owner.

title: Palmetto Man Pleads Guilty to Illegal Disposal of a Deceased Body
body: Press Release Palmetto Man Pleads Guilty to Illegal Disposal of a Deceased Body Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Tampa, Florida – Matthew Edward Zoladz (37, Palmetto) has pleaded guilty to one count of violating the Marine Protection, Research, and Sanctuaries Act, and one count of violating the Act to Prevent Pollution from Ships. He faces a maximum penalty of 15 years in federal prison. Zoladz will be sentenced on January 20, 2027. United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court documents, on or about December 7, 2022, Zoladz and Victim 1 engaged in drug use together, during which time Victim 1 overdosed and passed away. Zoladz drove around with Victim 1’s unconscious or deceased body in the front seat of his vehicle and took a video of Victim 1. On or about December 8, 2022, Zoladz was scheduled to work as a deckhand on a vessel. Prior to the departure of the vessel, Zoladz wrapped Victim 1’s body in a plastic trash bag and loaded Victim 1’s body onto the ship. That evening, while the ship was out at sea, Zoladz dumped the plastic trash bag containing Victim 1’s body into ocean waters. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Abigail K. King and E. Jackson Boggs, Jr. Updated November 3, 2026 Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: Seffner Man Sentenced to 24 years, Consecutive to 25-year State Prison Sentence, for Production and Distribution of Child Sexual Abuse Material
body: Press Release Seffner Man Sentenced to 24 years, Consecutive to 25-year State Prison Sentence, for Production and Distribution of Child Sexual Abuse Material Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Tampa, FL – Joel Reynolds (48, Seffner) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Thomas P. Barber to 24 years in federal prison for production, distribution, and possession of child sexual abuse material. The court ordered the sentence to run consecutive to Reynolds’s 25-year state prison sentence. Reynolds pleaded to the federal offenses on July 9, 2026. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court documents, law enforcement initiated an investigation into Reynolds after receiving a cyber tip from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children in November 2024. Further investigation revealed    Reynolds had produced child sexual abuse material and distributed at least one such image on a social media application. Law enforcement discovered Reynolds in possession of hundreds of videos depicting minors engaged in sexually explicit conduct on his devices. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Courtney Derry. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc. Updated November 3, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Florida, Middle

body: Press Release Fort Myers Man Sentenced to More than 21 Years in Federal Prison for Child Exploitation Offenses Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Fort Myers, Florida – Rudy Perez (41, Fort Myers) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Sheri Polster Chappell to 21 years and 8 months in federal prison for enticing minors to engage in sexual activity, receiving and possessing images and videos depicting the sexual abuse of children, and transferring obscene matter to a minor. Perez was found guilty on August 3, 2026, following a bench trial. Perez was also sentenced to a term of life of supervised release and ordered to register as a sex offender. United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court documents, between January and April 2022, Perez used a social media application to persuade, induce, and entice a minor to engage in sexual activity. In January 2025, a social media application made a Cybertipline Report to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) that Perez was involved with the online enticement of children for sexual acts. During the course of the investigation, law enforcement obtained a search warrant for Perez’s social media account. The FBI observed that Perez had enticed and solicited numerous other users who had identified themselves as children for sexually explicit images, and several minor children sent sexually explicit material to Perez at his request. Further, Perez sent photographs and sexually explicit videos and images of adults to numerous users who had identified themselves as children. Pursuant to a search warrant, Perez’s cellphone was seized and a subsequent forensic analysis revealed that Perez possessed child sexual abuse material, including numerous videos depicting the sexual abuse of minors. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Fort Myers Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force, which includes the Lee County Sheriff’s Office. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Yolande G. Viacava. This is another case brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc. Updated November 3, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: Federal grand jury indicts fourteen defendants in $370 million nationwide bank account takeover conspiracy
body: Press Release Federal grand jury indicts fourteen defendants in $370 million nationwide bank account takeover conspiracy Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas Ringleader attempted to flee U.S. before arrest at JFK airport gate DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould today announced that a federal grand jury indicted fourteen defendants, including allegedly corrupt insiders at major banking and telecommunication institutions, for allegedly orchestrating a sweeping nationwide bank‑account‑takeover conspiracy that targeted victims across the U.S. Muhamed Dieye, 35, of Dallas, known to associates by several aliases including “MJ,” “JayJay,” “Medici,” and “Lambomotion Tony,” is the leader and chief architect of the alleged conspiracy. Dieye and the thirteen co-defendants are charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and bank fraud, bank fraud, wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. A federal grand jury returned the 22-count indictment on Aug. 26. It was unsealed today after the arrest of Terrence Dudley a/k/a Willy Watkins, Brian Faceman in Florida, a key co-conspirator in the case. In addition to Dieye and Dudley, the indictment also charges: Maurice Rashad McDuffie, a/k/a Heavvvy Motion Saad Nashat Botros, a/k/a Felix Saucedo , Wesley Swipes , Wesley Swipes Sammed Kweku Okyne, a/k/a OKC , Paris Jawn Renaldo Santez Gaines, a/k/a BlackMigo , OsamaCapone , OsamaBin57 Alphonso Brndon Seke‑Horton, a/k/a The Wizard 302 Terry Leon Daniels Jr., a/k/a onedayrealsoon , Teazy Daniels Jamel Allen Small, a/k/a Paypawerk Kemar Fitzroy Needham, a/k/a Swap King Fx , kingzmanfx Kevin Brandon Flores Cazares, a/k/a John First B , First B (Call) Dylon Amari Ruby, a/k/a slimeyluhdude , AT&T Courtney Jane Sutton C.S. “North Texas is the financial services hub of America, and protecting Main Street families and investors is a top priority of this office,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “These defendants are charged with targeting the life savings of thousands of Americans, and the ringleader was stopped at the gate before he could flee. Target Main Street and we will pursue you with every tool available." A sophisticated, multi‑state identity‑theft ring According to the indictment, Dieye possessed a spreadsheet that contained detailed personal and business information for nearly 3,000 individual victims who collectively held over $373,000,000 across their bank accounts. From July 2023 through November 2024, the defendants allegedly conspired to obtain personal identifying information, produced and trafficked counterfeit identification documents, impersonated victims, manipulated victims’ phone lines by spoofing and SIM swapping, intercepted security codes and used corrupt insiders within banks and telecommunications companies to bypass authentication measures. Among the plays detailed in the indictment, the conspirators allegedly: Accessed or withdrew funds from victim accounts at Truist Bank, Bank of America, First Bank, Woodforest National Bank, JPMorgan Chase Bank, and Charles Schwab Conducted or attempted numerous fraudulent financial transactions, including an attempted $2,000,000 wire to the Emirates Islamic Bank Leveraged aliases referencing violent extremists and organized‑crime figures—such as OsamaCapone and OsamaBin57 —while executing and coordinating complex fraud plays Ringleader attempted to flee the United States Federal law enforcement, working closely with the U.S. Attorney’s Office, arrested Dieye after he allegedly attempted to flee the country. According to the government’s motion to revoke release: Dieye and his family vacated his Dallas residence, shipped most of his possessions to Kenya and traveled with his family to New York to board a one-way flight to Malaysia. Within hours of his flight, the U.S. Attorney’s Office and Diplomatic Security Service secured an arrest warrant. After scanning his boarding pass, Dieye allegedly physically resisted arrest, attempted to destroy one of his cell phones containing evidence that he was researching how to buy a home in Malaysia, and had to be subdued by multiple federal agents. While a Magistrate Court in the Eastern District of New York initially ordered Dieye released on bond, the United States immediately sought and obtained an emergency stay of his release. Dieye has since been transported to the Northern District of Texas, where he and several of his co-defendants remain in federal custody pending trial. If convicted, the defendants face a maximum penalty of 30 years in federal prison on the bank fraud conspiracy charge and 20 years in federal prison on the wire fraud conspiracy charge. Aggravated identity theft carries a mandatory sentence of two years’ imprisonment, consecutive to any other sentence imposed. The Diplomatic Security Service conducted the investigation with substantial assistance from the U.S. Secret Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Homeland Security Investigations, Drug Enforcement Administration, Customs and Border Protection, Social Security Administration Office of Inspector General, Federal Bureau of Investigation, National Insurance Crime Bureau, U.S. Embassy Dakar Senegal Office of Overseas Criminal Investigations, the Dallas Police Department, the Plano Police Department and the Collin County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael J. Murtha from the Major Crimes Section is prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation of criminal conduct, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. title: Former Berkeley County Sheriff’s Office Employee Admits Guilt in Multi-Million-Dollar Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Former Berkeley County Sheriff’s Office Employee Admits Guilt in Multi-Million-Dollar Fraud Scheme Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of West Virginia MARTINSBURG, WEST VIRGINIA – A former employee of the Berkeley County Sheriff’s Office has admitted her role in a years‑long fraud and embezzlement scheme that targeted vulnerable individuals and public funds, U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey announced today. Lisa Lee French, 48, of Martinsburg, admitted that between 2007 and October 2024, she conspired to steal cash payments collected by the Sheriff’s Office and to manipulate conservatorship and estate accounts overseen by the office. French acknowledged issuing fraudulent checks, forging signatures, misusing a sheriff’s signature stamp, and diverting funds for her personal benefit. “Fraud on this scale harms not only those directly targeted, but the entire Berkeley County community. We are committed to ensuring accountability and protecting the integrity of our public offices,” said U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey. The victims include Berkeley County taxpayers, individuals under conservatorship, and the Berkeley County Sheriff’s Office itself. According to court documents, the scheme involved more than 700 fraudulent transactions, over 550 of them forged checks, connected to at least 59 conservator bank accounts. In total, the fraud amounted to nearly $3 million. French has agreed to pay $2,737,932 in restitution to the identified victims. A second defendant, Barbara Gail Gooden, is awaiting trial on March 23, 2027. Read the original press release here . Senior Litigation Counsel Andrew Cogar is prosecuting the case. The investigation was conducted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Berkeley County Sheriff’s Office, and the West Virginia State Auditor’s Office. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the formation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”), which focuses on investigating and prosecuting fraud against the American public. This effort supports the President’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole‑of‑government initiative chaired by the Vice President to address fraud, waste, and abuse in federal benefit programs. U.S. Magistrate Judge Robert W. Trumble presided. Updated November 3, 2026 Topic Fraud Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - West Virginia, Northern

title: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
body: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI From infrastructure planning and transportation to public services, cities are using NVIDIA-powered applications to address local needs and expand capacity for the broader AI ecosystem. November 2, 2026 by Esther Lee 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge. Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used. Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin , NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own. Agentic AI for Cities From resident services to vision agents, cities are adopting NVIDIA agentic AI to deliver faster, more responsive public services. City teams don’t need a massive infrastructure investment to get started building these AI services: depending on the workload, NVIDIA RTX workstations or a small GPU system may be enough. In Spain, 1MillionBot combines open source ALIA models trained at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center with NVIDIA Nemotron and other models in resident-service agents for Madrid Digital (Comunidad de Madrid), Administració Oberta de Catalunya and 150+ deployments across Spain, handling municipal procedures, appointment requests, urban-planning incidents and service inquiries. In the San Francisco Bay Area , LiveX is bringing its AI City vision to life with NVIDIA Cosmos world models and Nemotron open models, and Omniverse and Metropolis libraries on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs. The interactive, conversational AI hosts understand people’s needs, provide answers and take action, and can be tailored to local languages and service needs in airports, hospitals, local events and other public spaces. Vision AI agents can turn existing city camera feeds into operational insights, helping teams identify mobility and safety issues and coordinate emergency responses across city services. In Wrocław, Poland , K2K is building shared AI infrastructure using NVIDIA accelerated computing, NVIDIA Cosmos world reasoning models, and NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) to transform existing camera streams into actionable intelligence for mobility, safety and event response — using the same infrastructure across several city functions. In Malaysia , ITMAX bundles infrastructure and agentic AI applications into long-term managed services for cities, including for traffic management. Built with reference to Cosmos, Nemotron and the Metropolis VSS blueprint, ITMAX’s SamurAI V2 vision agents are scaling on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs to support 17,000+ cameras by 2027. ITMAX integrates TeraSim, an open source traffic simulation platform from Laplace Intelligence , to test signal timing, reducing peak-hour corridor travel times by up to 26%. Plan and Operate Critical Infrastructure With Digital Twins Beyond public-facing services, digital twins can help cities expedite infrastructure planning, minimizing disruption to local communities. City digital twins can also serve as a real-time operational simulation to facilitate faster decision-making. At Dangote’s Lekki refinery in Nigeria, Honeywell Technologies’ Forge Plant Cognition uses Nemotron-powered AI agents to understand operational data. A digital twin of the plant and its processes, built using Omniverse libraries, is also planned to support simulation and training. The platform, built on Dell PowerEdge servers with NVIDIA RTX PRO accelerators, helps operators identify bottlenecks, anticipate equipment and process issues, and optimize plant performance. In Taiwan , Linker Vision and Dutch architecture firm MVRDV are using NVIDIA Omniverse and Nemotron to build environmental, social and governance agents that can assess the environmental impact of various urban planning scenarios, simulating 15-year outcomes of an urban forest canopy in 10 minutes — increasing design iteration speed from two weeks per iteration to less than an hour. Build a Broader Local AI Ecosystem Cities can extend AI to more services by building on infrastructure already in place and adding capacity. Shared resources and managed services can help extend those capabilities across departments and municipalities. At Morocco’s Tanger Med port, Cires Technologies is expanding a sovereign AI factory for planned applications in worker safety, congestion analysis, cargo routing and port operations. Cires Technologies is also building an ecosystem of application providers to develop local models and applications for ports and cities. Beyond city services, Barcelona Supercomputing Center’s AI Factory Accelerator Programme gives startups access to sovereign computing, technical support and training. BSC AI Factory also supports research and innovation for startups — spanning agriculture, medical imaging, knowledge access and speech services. Learn how NVIDIA and its ecosystem are bringing physical AI, agentic AI and local AI factories to cities worldwide at Smart City Expo World Congress, running Nov. 3-5 in Barcelona, where NVIDIA Vice President of EMEA Paolo Guglielmini will deliver a keynote address followed by a panel moderated by Charbel Aoun, director of smart city and spaces for EMEA at NVIDIA. title: AWS Weekly Roundup: GPT-6.1 Terra on Bedrock, Step Functions as agent tools, and more (November 2, 2026)
body: AWS Weekly Roundup: GPT-6.1 Terra on Bedrock, Step Functions as agent tools, and more (November 2, 2026) The agentic launches that stayed with me last week had nothing to do with how capable a model is. They were about reach. AWS Step Functions , which already orchestrates over 220 AWS services, can now be handed to an agent as a tool, so workflows teams already trust became callable without a rewrite. In the same week, the AI blog published how one engagement platform exposed roughly 400 internal API operations the same way. Neither story involves rebuilding anything, only describing what exists and letting the agent find it. The other thread was cost. OpenAI’s newest Terra model reached Amazon Bedrock priced well below the model beside it, and two post-quantum launches landed for a deadline nobody can put on a calendar yet. Now, let’s get into this week’s AWS news… Headlines OpenAI GPT-6.1 Terra is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock , and what interests me is where it sits rather than what it tops. Terra is the everyday-workload line of the GPT-6 family. In OpenAI’s Agents’ Last Exam evaluation it scored 15 percentage points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra, performed on par with GPT-6 Astra, and completed tasks more than three times faster than both. Those are OpenAI’s figures, not an independent test. The price is what I would check first: input and output tokens are at least 50% lower than GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-5.6 Terra. It takes up to 1 million input tokens with text and image input, and you can reach it from the Bedrock APIs or ChatGPT Work and Codex. AWS Step Functions workflows are now available as AI agent tools through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, which connects agents to tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The division of labor is the idea: the agent decides when to run a workflow and what input to pass; Step Functions runs each step exactly as you defined it. A support agent can trigger a refund, and the eligibility check, the manager approval, and the credit still happen in that order every time, because the ordering was never the model’s to improvise. Your existing Standard and Express workflows qualify as connector targets, and agents can also look up runs. It’s available in all Regions where AgentCore Gateway is, at standard rates. Last week’s launches Here are some launches and updates from this past week that caught my attention: AWS Key Management Service now supports ML-KEM for post-quantum key encapsulation – You can now establish a shared secret with a post-quantum algorithm using AWS KMS keys, with private keys in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated HSMs. All three NIST FIPS 203 parameter sets are supported through Encapsulate , which produces a random 32-byte shared secret and its ciphertext, and Decapsulate , which recovers it. The threat is harvest now, decrypt later: an adversary records today’s key exchange and recovers the secret once quantum computers are powerful enough. It’s available everywhere KMS runs except the Middle East (UAE and Bahrain) and China Regions. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL added post-quantum TLS key exchange the same week, on versions 18 and higher. AWS IAM Identity Center now supports cross-Region trusted identity propagation – You can now carry a user’s identity with their request to AWS services in another Region. This removes a genuine architectural constraint: trusted identity propagation used to require every service accessing that identity to sit in the same Region, which left two unappealing options, broad IAM roles that cannot distinguish individual users, or consolidating all your services into a single Region. Now the identity travels with the request automatically, so you grant access by user and group membership and audit who accessed what. It’s available at no additional cost everywhere IAM Identity Center runs. Amazon ECS now supports GPU sharing with NVIDIA Multi-Process Service (MPS) – You can now run multiple Amazon ECS tasks concurrently on a single NVIDIA GPU, the practical answer to work that only ever uses a fraction of one, like small-model inference and multi-model serving. You declare the GPU memory each container needs and can optionally cap its share of GPU compute, and ECS places tasks on GPUs with available capacity as your services scale, with no code changes. It works on ECS Managed Instances and ECS on Amazon EC2 , and on Managed Instances it watches the MPS control daemon and replaces the instance if it turns unhealthy. It’s available in all commercial and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. AWS Lambda supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) lazy loading for Lambda Managed Instances – You can now have AWS Lambda fetch only the files needed at each stage of startup instead of pulling a whole container image first, which AWS puts at up to 70% off container startup time. You create a SOCI index, push it to Amazon ECR , point the image URI at the indexed tag, and Lambda detects it automatically. The technique also reached Amazon SageMaker AI training and processing jobs, with benchmarks : lazy loading held at 3 to 11 seconds regardless of image size, against a median 3 minutes 42 seconds for a 13.2 GB image, a range they report as 8x to 46x. Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports Kubernetes Gateway API – You can now declare how traffic reaches your applications with Gateway and HTTPRoute resources on Amazon EKS without installing a separate controller, and EKS Auto Mode provisions and manages the underlying AWS load balancing infrastructure. You get HTTP and gRPC routing, cross-namespace routing, weighted traffic splitting, header-based routing, and automatic TLS certificate discovery through AWS Certificate Manager . Existing Ingress workloads keep working alongside them, so this is additive rather than a migration. Gateway API support is included with EKS Auto Mode; standard load balancing charges apply. For a full list of AWS announcements, be sure to keep an eye on the What’s New with AWS page. Other AWS news Here are some additional posts and resources that you might find interesting: How Nubank automated disaster recovery with the AWS DevOps Agent – Nubank serves more than 140 million customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, and classifies over 300 business flows as critical, each tested on a regulator’s schedule. Nubank reports that handing evidence collection and report writing to the AWS DevOps Agent cut a test cycle from about 4.3 hours to roughly 40 minutes, and quadrupled flow coverage in 2026 to more than 160. One execution terminated more than 900 EKS instances under synthetic traffic with AWS Fault Injection Service , producing the evidence its regulator needed. How MoEngage turned over 400 APIs into agent tools with AgentCore Gateway – Roughly 400 internal REST API operations, built by 25 teams, sitting in private VPCs across seven Regions, with tenant identity that could never become a parameter the model gets to set. MoEngage estimates the managed path saved about six months of platform engineering. The detail worth stealing: a full tool listing would have crossed 20,000 tokens per connection, so agents search for tools by describing a task instead of receiving the catalog. Reducing petabyte-scale S3 storage costs with evidence-based lifecycle rules – The hard part isn’t deciding to act, it’s knowing which data has gone cold and where it can safely live. This uses S3 Storage Lens groups and Storage Class Analysis to prove access patterns before moving anything. In the engagement described, 5.8 PB of logs in Amazon S3 Standard at approximately $241,000 per month showed an access ratio below 0.1% past 90 days, and a 90-day transition to Glacier Instant Retrieval cut the bill by roughly 70%, a figure the author ties to that workload. Upcoming AWS events Check your calendar and sign up for upcoming AWS events: AWS re:Invent – re:Invent returns to Las Vegas from November 30 to December 4, with more than 2,200 sessions. The event catalog is live and reserved seating is open, so register and claim your spots before they fill up. AWS Community Days – Community-led conferences planned and delivered by community leaders. The 2026 season is winding down as re:Invent approaches, so check the hub for what’s still on. Join the AWS Builder Center to connect with builders, share solutions, and access content that supports your development. Browse here for upcoming AWS-led in-person and virtual events and developer-focused events. That’s all for this week. Check back next Monday for another Weekly Roundup! – Daniel Abib This post is part of our Weekly Roundup series. Check back each week for a quick roundup of interesting news and announcements from AWS!
